title: Two heads are better than one: current landscape of integrating QSP and machine learning — An ISoP QSP SIG white paper by the working group on the integration of quantitative systems pharmacology and machine learning

content.abstract_summary: ISoP QSP SIG white paper from a 21-member, 18-organization working group (convened September 2019) on integrating QSP modeling and machine learning across drug development. Identifies four current integration categories (parameter estimation, model structure inference, dimension reduction, stochastic/virtual populations), presents four case studies, and concludes that QSP+ML is in early stages — moving from evaluating tools to building case studies — and serves as a foundation for future best-practices codification.
key_findings: Four categories of integrated QSP+ML approaches: (1) parameter estimation and extraction from qualitative/quantitative data; (2) model structure inference including logic networks and sensitivity analysis; (3) dimension reduction to extract key variables from high-dimensional data; (4) stochasticity and virtual populations including generative models for population parameter inference

SciML ('scientific machine learning') uses mechanistic priors inside the learning architecture — represented in the paper as the universal differential equation framework and PINNs. Key hybrid form: [Depot]' = -KaNN([Depot],[Central]) where the unknown nonlinear feedback is replaced by a neural network while the mechanistic scaffold is retained
DeepXDE (biologically-informed neural networks) showed local optimization 100× to 10,000× more expensive than traditional approaches — a significant computational limitation for PINNs in QSP settings

Case study 1 (thrombosis): QSP model of coagulation pathway linked to ML event prediction; real-world event rate data at multiple doses used to train event prediction algorithm; supported clinical development of anti-coagulants

Case study 2 (drug-induced liver injury): QSP model with 112 coupled differential and algebraic equations; NLP used to identify gene-expression connections from literature; ML + QSP predicted relative impact of mechanistic hepatotoxic perturbations

Case study 3 (T cell differentiation): logic-based QSP model of T cell signaling; ML classification of dynamic response identified novel complex multi-fate T cell phenotypes and cytokine dosage-timing effects on T cell fate

Operational guidance: 'AI hierarchy of needs' (after Maslow) — must satisfy collect data → store → integrate → explore → model → report before ML is possible; most pharma companies are at the AI Outsourcing or ML-capable stage, not AI-driven

'The current state of the art does not include fully integrated hybrid QSP + ML models' — case studies are ML-assisted QSP modeling, not true hybrids; future goal is iteratively uncovering black box mechanisms through systematic analysis

Surrogate ML models trained on QSP simulation outputs are used to reduce computational burden for parameter space characterization and sensitivity analysis — an area where QSP and PMx practice already converge

Feature selection (FS) + QSP integration: two strategies: (a) FS first to identify minimal physiologically meaningful feature subset for QSP parameterization; (b) build full QSP model first, then apply dimension reduction — both aim for parsimonious models that balance interpretability and complexity
limitations: Scoped entirely within QSP (systems-scale mechanistic models, ODE/PDE/logic networks) rather than NLME-based pharmacometrics (compartmental PK/PD) — MCS WG operates in PMx space, so direct methodological overlap is partial

No fully integrated hybrid QSP+ML models existed at time of writing (2022) — all case studies are 'ML-assisted QSP', not true hybrids; the mechanistic and ML components are largely trained/estimated separately

DeepXDE/PINNs are 100-10,000× more computationally expensive than traditional ODE solvers for biologically-informed neural networks — practical scalability to clinical development timelines is unresolved
High-quality, high-volume clinical data remains the primary bottleneck for QSP+ML; decentralized trial data, wearables, and collaborative warehouses are emerging but data harmonization is unsolved

QSP models are 'chronically under-determined due to limited clinical and preclinical pharmacology data' — ML does not resolve this fundamental identifiability challenge; the paper does not address structural or practical identifiability of hybrid components
Published 2022 based on 2019–2021 scoping — landscape has shifted substantially with foundation models, SciML advances (Julia ecosystem), and regulatory developments since then

extracted_claims.text: "The current state of the art does not include fully integrated hybrid QSP + ML models. The case studies presented are ML-assisted QSP modeling, using ML to address weaknesses of QSP models."

"The integration of QSP and ML is still in its early stages of moving from evaluating available technical tools to building case studies. Such integration offers multiple advantages from providing data-driven QSP model parameterization, to imposing a QSP model framework to increase interpretability of high dimensional data and fully data-driven QSP model structure discovery."

"ML can be oversold as a magic solution to every problem, but it is not... The right framework to think through is how to better understand an organization's decisions, how those decisions are currently made, when are they going to be made in the future, what information would be helpful to have at the time of the decision being made, and then, finally, how the data can be collected, processed, analyzed, and translated into an insight to inform that decision."

A comparison of standard ODE solver based parameter estimation with the DeepXDE package used in Biologically-Informed Neural Networks showed local optimization of parameters was 100× to 10,000× more expensive than traditional approaches.

"[A] QSP model describing the mechanisms of necrosis, steatosis and cholestasis comprising 112 coupled differential and algebraic equations were constructed" — then linked with gene-expression ML for hepatotoxicity prediction.

gaps_addressed: Provides the sister SIG (QSP) taxonomy for hybrid mechanistic-ML integration — the four categories (parameter estimation, model structure, dimension reduction, stochastic/virtual) are directly mappable to WG Pillar 1 scope decisions; MCS WG should cite this taxonomy and clarify which categories apply at the PMx (NLME) scale vs. QSP (network) scale

The '100-10,000× more expensive' finding for PINNs/DeepXDE is a key quantitative limitation that motivates the iNODE approach (campo_manzanares_2026) — the two papers together frame the problem-and-solution arc for Pillar 1
The 'fully integrated hybrid QSP+ML models do not yet exist' conclusion (2022) establishes a clear benchmark: has this changed by 2026? The WG scoping paper should assess this explicitly
The AI hierarchy of needs framework is directly usable in the Pillar 4 position paper — it provides a principled framework for assessing organizational readiness for GenAI in drug development
Virtual population + ML (GAN/normalizing flow) methods discussed in Category 4 overlap with Pillar 4 (generative models) and inform the synthetic patient validation gap the WG has identified
